draft.title: Notification timing + re-engagement cadence (perceptual/display angle)
draft.principle_summary: Cadence and copy-framing for reminders are fully owned by PSYCHOLOGY law 14 (do not re-derive). The remaining non-behavioral question is real: platform notification systems (Android, iOS) formally split visual/audible interruption weight by message class, independent of send frequency. That gives Solen a display-only rule that RATIONALE currently lacks: a transactional notification (booking confirmation, appointment reminder) earns the loud/heads-up treatment (system push banner, sound, app-icon badge increment); a non-transactional nudge (rebooking suggestion, Inspo digest, promo) is displayed quiet-only (in-app banner or the already-locked Toast recipe), never a push banner, never an app-icon badge. This is a routing rule from message CLASS to DISPLAY WEIGHT, not a cadence rule, so it does not duplicate law 14.

draft.solen_current: RATIONALE.md already covers the TOAST component's own visual mechanics: section 14 "Toast auto-dismiss and max visible" (RATIONALE.md:474-479, grounding LOCKFILE:604-614) locks 4s auto-dismiss / max-3-visible as house convention (CONV), and section 14's "Entrance recipes table" (RATIONALE.md:654-657) locks toast/chip entrance as a slide-up-and-settle "glide", explicitly reasoning that "chrome like toasts stays understated." Section 20 "Domain 16: states and feedback" (RATIONALE.md:735-749) covers the state matrix and perceived-performance mechanics but does not touch notification/reminder display. There is no RATIONALE section anywhere that names a rule for CHOOSING which surface (system push banner vs app badge vs in-app toast/banner) a given notification uses, and no rule distinguishing the display weight of a transactional message from a re-engagement nudge. PSYCHOLOGY.md law 14 (line 55) owns cadence and copy-framing for reminders ("Non-transactional pushes cap at 2-3/week; settings split by category, Buchungen ON, Angebote/Inspo OFF by default") but is silent on the VISUAL form each notification class should take once it fires.
draft.gap: Missing domain: RATIONALE has a locked component (Toast) and a locked cadence law (PSYCHOLOGY 14) but no rule connecting message CLASS to DISPLAY SURFACE/WEIGHT. Without it, an engineer wiring a new notification type (e.g. a rebooking nudge, or a booking-confirmed push) has no documented default for whether it should be a system push banner, an app-icon badge increment, or the in-app Toast, and no reasoning for why those three surfaces exist as a ladder rather than being interchangeable.
draft.proposed_addition:
## Domain 24: Notification display weight (message class to surface, not cadence)

DECISION: notification DISPLAY SURFACE is chosen by message class, in a fixed three-rung ladder: (1) transactional and time-critical (booking confirmed, appointment reminder, payment failed) gets the loudest available surface, an OS-level push banner with sound plus an app-icon badge increment; (2) transactional but not time-critical (a document ready, a review request) gets a push banner without a forced badge increment; (3) non-transactional or re-engagement (rebooking suggestion, Inspo digest, promo) is confined to the in-app surface only, the already-locked Toast recipe (LOCKFILE:604-614) or an in-app banner, never a system push and never an app-icon badge. This rule decides WHICH SURFACE a notification uses. It does NOT decide how often class-3 notifications fire; that stays PSYCHOLOGY law 14's 2-3/week cap and per-category opt-in/opt-out defaults, cross-referenced not re-derived.

FORCES: a system push banner and an app-icon badge are the loudest tools an app has, interrupting whatever the user is doing outside the app entirely; using them for low-value content trains the user to dismiss or mute the channel, which then also mutes the transactional messages the user actually needs (booking confirmations, reminders). Conversely, under-using the loud surface for a genuinely time-critical message (a payment failure) risks a missed action with a real cost.

OPTIMIZES FOR: preserving the push channel's signal-to-noise so a transactional push keeps its attention-earning power; letting a non-transactional nudge exist without paying the cost of a system-level interruption or a persistent badge the user cannot act on to clear.

SACRIFICES: a non-transactional nudge confined to in-app Toast/banner is only seen if and when the user opens the app, so a rebooking suggestion cannot itself pull a lapsed user back in; that job stays with whatever separate low-frequency channel PSYCHOLOGY law 14 already governs (SMS/email/allowed push slots), not with the in-app surface.

BOUNDARY: this rule governs SURFACE CHOICE only. It does not set send times, does not set the weekly cap, does not set copy framing, and it does not reopen the Toast component's own locked visual recipe (LOCKFILE:604-614, TASTE_LOG V3-D462); a class-3 notification that lands in-app still renders through the existing Toast component unchanged.

MECHANIC: Android's notification design system enforces exactly this class-to-surface split structurally, an importance/channel model where "Transactional" can stay on while "Promotions/Reminders" is muted, and where only High/Urgent channels earn a heads-up (sound plus floating) presentation (CONV, named platform convention, developer.android.com). Apple's Human Interface Guidelines independently converge on the badge half of this: a badge must supplement, never carry, critical information by itself, and a custom UI element must never impersonate a system badge (T1, developer.apple.com, System experiences: Notifications). Bailey and Konstan (2006) and the follow-on Iqbal and Bailey CHI 2008 work establish that an interruption's cost is measurable (resumption lag, error rate, reported annoyance) and is lower at natural task breakpoints, which is the underlying reason a low-value message should not claim the same interruption-cost budget as a high-value one (T2).

SOURCE: Android Developers notification channel/importance docs (developer.android.com); Apple Human Interface Guidelines, System experiences: Notifications (developer.apple.com); Bailey and Konstan 2006, Computers in Human Behavior; Iqbal and Bailey, CHI 2008; cross-reference PSYCHOLOGY.md law 14 (cadence, opt-out data, per-category defaults, already sourced there, not re-derived here); Solen LOCKFILE.md:604-614 and TASTE_LOG V3-D462 (Toast recipe, unchanged by this entry).
draft.taste_lab_probe: Not applicable in the generative-prior sense (this stream is tag=net-new, not generative-gap): there is no numeric band to calibrate. If a probe is wanted before this ships as a build task, the checkable question is behavioral, not aesthetic: does routing rebooking nudges through in-app-only Toast (versus a push banner) measurably change the push-channel's opt-out rate for Buchungen notifications over a few weeks. That is an operational A/B, not a taste-lab session, and would live under PSYCHOLOGY's measurement practice, not RATIONALE's.

verified.title: Notification timing + re-engagement cadence (perceptual/display angle)

claim_verdicts.claim: Android's notification design system ties visual/audible interruption to an importance level (High/Urgent = sound + heads-up floating banner, Default = sound only, Low = silent, None = no status-bar entry), and lets a user mute a Promotions/Reminders channel while keeping Transactional notifications on.
claim_verdicts.note: Verified directly against developer.android.com/training/notify-user/channels. Exact mapping confirmed: Urgent (IMPORTANCE_HIGH) = sound + heads-up; High (IMPORTANCE_DEFAULT) = sound only, no heads-up; Medium (IMPORTANCE_LOW) = silent; Low/None (IMPORTANCE_MIN/NONE) = silent, drawer-only. The per-channel mute-while-keeping-others-on capability is a real Android platform feature (channels are independently user-mutable); the specific channel NAMES (Promotions/Reminders vs Transactional) are an app's own naming choice, not an Android-mandated taxonomy, so the sentence is accurate as long as it's read as 'the platform supports this split,' not 'Android requires these channel names.' Tier CONV is honest (platform convention, not a research finding).

claim_verdicts.claim: Apple's Human Interface Guidelines state a badge should supplement a notification, not carry critical information by itself, must be kept in sync with real unread state, and a custom UI element must never mimic the appearance of a system badge.
claim_verdicts.note: Two of three sub-claims verified against Apple's HIG System experiences: Notifications page: 'badging should be used to supplement notifications, not to denote critical information' and 'keep badges up to date, update your app's badge as soon as the corresponding information is read.' The third sub-claim, that HIG explicitly bars a custom UI element from mimicking a system badge's appearance, could NOT be independently confirmed in Apple's notifications HIG text via search; it may be conflating a general badge-component design-system convention (avoid visual confusion between components) with an Apple-specific rule. Cut that clause from the verified addition rather than cite it as Apple's stated position.

claim_verdicts.claim: Delivering a notification at a task breakpoint (a natural pause) lowers measured interruption cost (resumption lag, error rate, reported annoyance) versus delivering it mid-task; effects vary by task type (faster for perceptual/stimulus-driven tasks than for slower semantic ones).
claim_verdicts.note: Both papers are real and correctly attributed (Bailey and Konstan 2006, Computers in Human Behavior, DOI 10.1016/j.chb.2005.12.009; Iqbal and Bailey CHI 2008). The core claim, that breakpoint-timed delivery reduces measured interruption cost versus mid-task delivery, is confirmed: Bailey/Konstan found peripheral-task interruptions during a primary task cost 3-27% more time, 2x errors, and 31-106% more annoyance versus interruptions between tasks; Iqbal/Bailey 2008 found breakpoint scheduling reduces frustration and reaction time versus immediate delivery. The 'perceptual/stimulus-driven vs semantic task type' distinction could NOT be confirmed as coming from either cited paper; it more closely resembles the coarse-vs-fine breakpoint granularity finding from a DIFFERENT paper (Adamczyk and Bailey, CHI 2004, 'If not now, when?'), which is not in the source list. Drop the task-type qualifier from anything presented as coming from the two cited sources.

claim_verdicts.claim: Solen's Toast component (light white pill, colored circle badge icon, bottom-docked, 4s auto-dismiss, max 3 visible) is the LOCKED in-app quiet-notification recipe.
claim_verdicts.note: Grep-confirmed: LOCKFILE.md has a Toast/Toaster section starting at line 607, inside the cited 604-614 range. Internal house convention, correctly tiered.

claim_verdicts.claim: Non-transactional pushes cap at 2-3 per week; volume (not content) drives opt-outs, measured at 46% opting out at a 2-5/week send rate.
claim_verdicts.note: Draft explicitly scopes this as a cross-reference to PSYCHOLOGY.md law 14, already sourced and presumably vetted in that stream's own verify pass, not re-derived in S23. Neither the 2-3/week cap nor the 46% figure appears on the myth_screen never-cite list, so nothing here trips the screen. Not independently re-verified in this pass since the draft correctly declines to re-derive it; flagged in residual_risks so the owner knows this stream did not re-check law 14's own sourcing.

myths_caught: "perceptual/stimulus-driven vs semantic" task-type breakpoint distinction attributed to Bailey/Konstan 2006 and Iqbal/Bailey CHI 2008: not confirmable from either cited paper, resembles a different paper's (Adamczyk and Bailey 2004) coarse/fine breakpoint finding misattributed here. Dropped from the mechanic reasoning.

Apple HIG 'a custom UI element must never mimic the appearance of a system badge': not confirmable as an Apple HIG statement, softened to only the two confirmed clauses (supplement-not-critical, kept-in-sync).

verified.residual_risks:
Two corrections were made to the draft's sourcing: (1) the Apple HIG claim about a custom element never mimicking a system badge could not be verified and was cut, keep only the two confirmed HIG clauses if this ships; (2) the perceptual-vs-semantic task-type qualifier on the breakpoint research was dropped as unattributable to the two cited papers, it likely belongs to a different, uncited paper (Adamczyk and Bailey 2004). Neither correction weakens the core DECISION, both were supporting mechanic detail.

The 2-3/week cap and 46% opt-out figure are carried forward from PSYCHOLOGY law 14 as a cross-reference and were NOT independently re-verified in this pass, per the draft's own scoping. If law 14's own sourcing for that 46% figure has not itself been through an adversarial verify pass, that is a gap upstream of S23, not introduced here.

Lock tension for the owner to decide, not resolved here: this domain proposes a badge-increment rule (class 1 gets an app-icon badge) but Solen's own product does not yet have a documented decision on WHEN the badge count resets or what it counts (unread notifications vs. unread bookings vs. something else). That is a QUESTIONS.md candidate, not something to invent here. Also worth flagging to the owner: the three-rung ladder assumes iOS/Android push infrastructure is already wired for per-class routing, if it currently sends one undifferentiated push type, this domain implies a build task, not just a documentation entry.
